key_insight: TREX automates the entire LLM fine-tuning lifecycle by using a multi-agent, tree-based exploration framework that orchestrates planning (Researcher) and execution (Executor) to discover, run, and refine training pipelines with minimal human intervention.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of automating complex, multi-step LLM training workflows—requirement analysis, open-domain literature/data discovery, experiment orchestration, hyperparameter/search strategy exploration, and iterative refinement—that normally demand extensive manual effort and expertise.
method: Multi-agent architecture: a Researcher agent for requirement analysis, literature/data research, and candidate strategy generation; an Executor agent for dataset assembly, training runs, evaluation, and enactment of plans.
Tree-based exploration: hierarchical branching of candidate training pipelines (data, objectives, hyperparameters, augmentations), with iterative pruning and selection driven by evaluation feedback.
Full lifecycle automation: end-to-end orchestration from requirement spec → open-domain research → experiment scheduling → metric-driven iteration and convergence.
impact: TREX speeds up and standardizes LLM fine-tuning, lowering the barrier for practitioners to experiment at scale, improving reproducibility, and enabling faster deployment of task-specific models with less manual tuning.
